Third-party notices for assets/vendor/flubber.min.js
====================================================

flubber.min.js is the unmodified browser build of flubber 0.4.2 (build/flubber.min.js in the
npm package, 53,509 bytes). The ui pages use it to interpolate between SVG paths. It runs only
in the local page renderer and loads nothing from the network. The flubber licence is also in
flubber.LICENSE.

The build bundles code from six other open-source libraries. The build has no licence comments,
so each library was identified from its code in the build. The versions come from the flubber
0.4.2 dependency ranges, the dates of the releases in those ranges, and code differences between
releases.

  Library               Version         Licence        Copyright
  flubber               0.4.2           MIT            Copyright (c) 2017 Noah Veltman
  svgpath               2.2.1           MIT            Copyright (C) 2013-2015 by Vitaly Puzrin
  svg-path-properties   0.2.1 or 0.2.2  MIT            Copyright (c) 2016 Roger Veciana i Rovira
  earcut                2.1.1           ISC            Copyright (c) 2016, Mapbox
  topojson-client       3.0.0           BSD-3-Clause   Copyright (c) 2012-2016, Michael Bostock
  d3-array              1.2.0 or 1.2.1  BSD-3-Clause   Copyright 2010-2016 Mike Bostock
  d3-polygon            1.0.3           BSD-3-Clause   Copyright 2010-2016 Mike Bostock

Notes:
- svg-path-properties declares ISC in its package metadata, but its LICENSE file is MIT. The MIT
  text from that file is reproduced below. Its arc-to-curve code is taken from svgpath.
- topojson-client and the d3 modules moved to ISC in later major versions. The versions in this
  build are BSD-3-Clause.
- The build uses these parts: svgpath (path parser, transforms, arc conversion), svg-path-
  properties (path length and point-at-length), earcut (triangulation), topojson-client (feature,
  merge, stitch, neighbors, bisect, transform), d3-array (ascending, bisector) and d3-polygon
  (area, centroid, length).

The licence texts follow, each with its own copyright line.
